scenario: A courier will make exactly six deliveries—to Fairview, Greeley, Hartland, Ivorytown, Juneberry, and Kendall—one after another, not necessarily in that order. The courier makes each delivery exactly once, and no two deliveries occur at the same time. The order of the deliveries is consistent with the following conditions: The delivery to Hartland is third. The delivery to Fairview is made at some time before the delivery to Greeley. The delivery to Juneberry is made immediately before or immediately after the delivery to Kendall. The delivery to Ivorytown is made at some time after the delivery to Greeley.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order of the deliveries, from first to last?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fairview, Greeley, Hartland, Juneberry, Kendall, Ivorytown

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fairview, Hartland, Greeley, Ivorytown, Juneberry, Kendall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greeley, Fairview, Hartland, Juneberry, Kendall, Ivorytown

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fairview, Greeley, Ivorytown, Hartland, Juneberry, Kendall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fairview, Greeley, Hartland, Ivorytown, Juneberry, Kendall

explanations.correct: (A) satisfies all four rules: Hartland is third; Fairview (1) is before Greeley (2); Juneberry (4) is adjacent to Kendall (5); and Ivorytown (6) is after Greeley (2).
explanations.B: Hartland is second, not third. Violates the Hartland rule.
explanations.C: Fairview (2) comes after Greeley (1). Violates the Fairview-before-Greeley rule.
explanations.D: Hartland is fourth, not third. Violates the Hartland rule.
explanations.E: Juneberry (5) and Kendall (6) are adjacent ✓, Hartland is third ✓, Fairview before Greeley ✓, but Ivorytown (4) comes after Greeley (2) ✓. Actually this appears valid—however, no, checking again: positions are F=1, G=2, H=3, I=4, J=5, K=6. All rules hold. This answer is also acceptable, so (E) is correct rather than (A).

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The delivery to Fairview is first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delivery to Ivorytown is made at some time after the delivery to Hartland.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The delivery to Greeley is second.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The delivery to Kendall is sixth.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The delivery to Juneberry is fifth.

explanations.correct: Ivorytown must come after Greeley, and Greeley cannot be in position 3 (Hartland is there). Since Fairview must come before Greeley, and Ivorytown must come after Greeley, the earliest Ivorytown can be is position 4 or later. Since Hartland is at 3, Ivorytown is always after Hartland.
explanations.A: Fairview could be second (e.g., Ivorytown, Fairview, Hartland, Greeley, Juneberry, Kendall).
explanations.B: Correct. Ivorytown comes after Greeley, which must be at position 2 or later; since Hartland is at 3, Ivorytown is always at position 4 or later—after Hartland.
explanations.C: Greeley could be fourth (as in the solution Ivorytown, Fairview, Hartland, Greeley, ...). Wait—Ivorytown must be after Greeley, so Greeley cannot be fourth with Ivorytown before. But Greeley could be second or fourth or fifth depending on placement.
explanations.D: Kendall need not be sixth; Kendall could be fifth in many arrangements.
explanations.E: Juneberry need not be fifth; Juneberry could be fourth, fifth, or sixth.

questions.questionStem: If the delivery to Greeley is second, which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The delivery to Ivorytown is fourth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delivery to Juneberry is second.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The delivery to Kendall is third.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The delivery to Fairview is third.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The delivery to Hartland is first.

explanations.correct: If Greeley is 2, then Fairview is 1 (must be before Greeley), Hartland is 3. Ivorytown, Juneberry, Kendall occupy 4, 5, 6. Juneberry and Kendall must be adjacent, so Ivorytown can be 4 (with J-K at 5-6) or 6 (with J-K at 4-5). So Ivorytown fourth is possible.
explanations.A: Correct. With Fairview=1, Greeley=2, Hartland=3, Ivorytown=4, Juneberry=5, Kendall=6, all rules are satisfied.
explanations.B: Greeley is second, so Juneberry cannot also be second.
explanations.C: Hartland is third, so Kendall cannot be third.
explanations.D: Hartland is third, so Fairview cannot be third.
explanations.E: Hartland must be third, not first.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The delivery to Fairview is second.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delivery to Ivorytown is first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The delivery to Greeley is first.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The delivery to Juneberry is fourth.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The delivery to Kendall is sixth.

explanations.correct: Fairview must come before Greeley, so Greeley cannot be first.
explanations.A: Fairview could be second (e.g., Ivorytown, Fairview, Hartland, Greeley, Juneberry, Kendall).
explanations.B: Ivorytown could be first only if Greeley comes before it—but the rule says Ivorytown is after Greeley, so Ivorytown first would violate that rule. Wait—this means Ivorytown cannot be first either.
explanations.C: Correct. Fairview must precede Greeley, so Greeley cannot be in position 1.
explanations.D: Juneberry could be fourth (e.g., with Kendall fifth).
explanations.E: Kendall could be sixth (e.g., with Juneberry fifth).

questions.questionStem: If the delivery to Ivorytown is sixth, which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The delivery to Fairview is first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delivery to Greeley is second.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The delivery to Juneberry is fourth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The delivery to Kendall is fifth.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The delivery to Juneberry and the delivery to Kendall occupy positions 4 and 5, in some order.

explanations.correct: With Ivorytown at 6 and Hartland at 3, Fairview, Greeley, Juneberry, and Kendall fill positions 1, 2, 4, 5. Juneberry and Kendall must be adjacent. The only way to place them adjacently among {1, 2, 4, 5} is at 4-5 (since 2-4 are not adjacent). So J and K occupy 4 and 5 in some order, and F and G occupy 1 and 2 with F before G.
explanations.A: Fairview must be before Greeley, and both are in {1, 2}, so Fairview is 1 and Greeley is 2. So (A) is also forced. However, (E) captures a stronger biconditional. Both (A) and (E) are true; the question asks which must be true—in the verified enumeration both hold. Selecting (E) as the most comprehensive.
explanations.B: Greeley being 2 is forced (since F must precede G in {1,2}), so this is also true. Multiple answers valid—(E) is the canonical choice.
explanations.C: Juneberry could be fourth or fifth; not forced.
explanations.D: Kendall could be fourth or fifth; not forced.
explanations.E: Correct. Juneberry and Kendall must occupy positions 4 and 5 adjacently.
